item.text: The parser behavior is converging on a very simple grammar: detect `"://"` if present, strip `#fragment`, split once on `?`, strip userinfo via `@`, then take host up to the first `:` and parse a numeric prefix from the port field. I’m checking just a couple of ambiguous delimiter cases, then I’ll write the Rust modules and wire the Cargo binary.

item.text:
Implemented the Rust port as a complete Cargo project in [Cargo.toml](/output/Cargo.toml:1), with the required entrypoint in [test5.rs](/output/test5.rs:1) and modular parser code in [src/url_parser.rs](/output/src/url_parser.rs:1), [src/url_parser/authority.rs](/output/src/url_parser/authority.rs:1), and [src/url_parser/split.rs](/output/src/url_parser/split.rs:1). The implementation is a black-box re-creation of the observed C++ behavior, not a standards-based URL parser.

It builds successfully with both `cargo build --release` and `rustc --edition=2021 test5.rs -O -o test5`. Executables are present at `/output/test5` and `/output/target/release/test5`. I also verified byte-for-byte output parity against `/workspace/dataset/test5_executable` across the provided examples, many edge cases, and the no-argument exit path (`exit code 1`).
